powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File windows-agent-wait-spike.ps1 -Target 127.0.0.1 -Port <port> -User <fixture-user> (run twice on the owner's PC by the orchestrator's PC agent: first as committed at fe57c1d6, which measured nothing, then with $pipePath = '//./pipe/' + $pipe, the script's form now)

observed_result.macos: ssh and git ls-remote completed a real publickey login with the identities answer delayed 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 s (sshd LoginGraceTime 120) and 65 s (LoginGraceTime 0); at 125 s with LoginGraceTime 120 both failed (ssh exit 255, git exit 128) because sshd closed the connection; no client agent timeout up to 65 s. 52 agent messages (types 27 session-bind@openssh.com, 11, 13 only), none carrying the working directory, the repository name or the canary. session-bind arrived before REQUEST_IDENTITIES on every connection.
observed_result.linux: As macOS: every delay up to 65 s succeeded for ssh and git; 125 s failed by the server's LoginGraceTime (raw unauthenticated probe closed after 120.007 s); 52 agent messages, no directory context; session-bind first.
observed_result.windows: ssh and git ls-remote received the identities answer (a fake agent answering zero identities) at every delay, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 s, after the delay plus 0.10-0.19 s, with no timeout; the logins then failed by design (ssh exit 255, git exit 128). Every run sent exactly two agent messages, session-bind@openssh.com (27) then REQUEST_IDENTITIES (11); none of the 28 carried the working directory or the canary. The first run (-o IdentityAgent=\\.\pipe\...) reached no agent at all: OpenSSH_for_Windows 9.5p2 drops one backslash from that value.

limitations: Whether a client agent timeout exists above 65 s (macOS, Linux) or above 30 s (Windows, the longest delay tested) is not determined: the 125 s runs were ended by the server first.
Measurement spike on scratch fixtures (disposable keys, a disposable ssh-agent or the script's fake agent, a loopback-only sshd); no product code ran.
On Windows the fake agent answers zero identities, so the login itself fails by design; the measured facts are that the answer was received and how long the client waited for it.
The Windows results are redacted copies (account and PC names replaced, LF line endings); the unredacted originals stay on the PC.
